local_coconet_health.description: Inspect this project’s local processing, replica and search coverage when an operation is blocked or the user asks about sync. Background issues do not imply a selected source is unavailable; use its Read/Pull result. Detailed logs are available through coconet projection status --json and coconet diagnostics list.

local_read_project_work_graph.description: Read the verified local project DAG and committed Session open items without downloading conversations. Inspect processing coverage and node relations status: pending relations are not confirmed independent roots. Select a node and its exact source for pull_session before relying on implementation or verification claims. Follow next_cursor to inspect additional pages; restart when the project changes between pages.

local_search_work.description: Search accepted node text, Library notes and locally indexed user/assistant conversation text in the project connected to this folder (coconet connect). query requires 1–4000 nonblank characters and at most 64 whitespace-separated literal terms; matches any term. limit is 1–20, default 10; use next_cursor for more results. No model call or network download is needed. Inspect index coverage and revision: missing or unindexed copies make results partial. content_matches contain an exact source, turn_id, ordinal and snippet; work_node_ids may be empty while processing is pending. Repeated cumulative prefixes are deduplicated. Read the selected compact source before relying on detailed claims. Restart without a cursor if the query, graph or index changes.

local_pull_session.description: Read an exact retained source into compact_path, using verified local copies first. Copy source (session_id, version) from graph or search results, and include work_node_id when selecting a node. Without a node only compact reading is allowed. include_artifact and native continuation require a valid work node. A changed node source requires a refreshed selection. Missing temporary cloud content enters peer repair; waiting is not successful download. Runtime replicates retained project Sessions in the background.

local_list_library_entries.description: Browse explicitly collected fixed nodes, notes and sources in the local project Library without downloading conversations. Follow next_cursor at the same project revision; restart the listing when the graph changes. Collection does not imply completion.

local_add_session_to_library.description: Only on explicit user request, collect a selected own Work Node and its exact source from the local graph. Supply request_id, work_node_id, source and an optional note. This seals the node at the selected version; collection does not mark work complete. Reuse the same request_id and all original arguments after timeout. A changed source requires refreshing the graph and a new request_id. This tool does not capture an unprocessed live Session.

local_fork_session.description: Only on explicit user request, create a separate Session in the current Agent (Codex, Claude or Cursor) from a selected exact DAG node source. Same-Agent Fork preserves native history; cross-Agent Fork transfers effective user/assistant text only, excluding tools, reasoning and media. Supply a stable request_id, work_node_id and source. Reuse all original arguments after timeout; retries preserve the child identity. This uses verified local history, downloads missing content as needed, preserves workspace files and source history, and returns native_session_id plus a resume command. Success means the local Session is ready; project synchronization continues in the background. Inherited dialogue is saved as baseline, not new work; subsequent conversation is processed after that baseline synchronizes. End work in this conversation and give the user the resume command.

local_remove_session_from_library.description: Only on explicit user request, remove a selected own entry from Session Library using a stable request_id, work_node_id and exact source. Reuse all original arguments after timeout. This changes the bookmark only: the sealed DAG node and fixed conversation source are retained. It does not delete native history, reopen the node or mark work complete.
